verifications.formula: layers x swaps_per_layer x sigma3_per_swap = total sigma3 gates

verifications.description: The obfuscation mechanism uses only sigma3 gates (reversible) and XOR. No hash functions, discrete log, or factoring assumptions are made. Security relies on physical space-time uncertainty, not algebraic hardness.

verifications.verification: Side-Channel Resistance via Moving Computation — Slides 7 & 15
verifications.description: The obfuscated_xor module changes which physical wire carries the XOR result based on control bit b. The circuit_obfuscation module moves p4/p5 group computation between u/z and v/w outputs. Power traces differ per execution without rewiring.

sigma3 with b=1 routes f-result to location A and g-result to location B. With b=0 the assignments swap. b can be randomized each invocation, making the physical location of computation unpredictable. A proprietary algorithm can be hidden inside the obfuscated circuit.

verifications.verification: XOR Gate Requires 4 sigma3 Gates — Page 26
verifications.description: 4-NAND XOR: N=NAND(A,B), AN=NAND(A,N), BN=NAND(B,N), XOR=NAND(AN,BN). Each NAND uses 1 sigma3 gate. Total: 4 sigma3 gates.

verifications.verification: Permutation Complexity: at most n-1 Swaps — Page 26
verifications.description: Any permutation of n bits needs at most n-1 transpositions (swaps). For AES S-Box, n=48 bits per layer (8-bit coefficients x 6 terms). Paper uses 7 swaps/layer which is well within the n-1=47 bound.

Kerckhoffs' principle assumes the algorithm is known but the key is secret. Self-modifiable circuits VIOLATE this assumption advantageously: even knowing the full circuit design, an adversary cannot predict WHICH physical gate executes the computation on any given run, because the control bit b is randomized each invocation. The Red Queen hypothesis applies: the circuit constantly changes to maintain security fitness, like organisms evolving to survive.
verifications.red_queen_analogy: Organisms change to maintain survival fitness — circuits change location to maintain security

verifications.description: The sigma3 gate implements CSWAP (Controlled-SWAP), identical to the Fredkin gate (Fredkin & Toffoli, 1982). The Fredkin gate is a standard quantum computing primitive. Since ALL quantum gates must be unitary (reversible), sigma3-based circuits compile directly to quantum circuits with no modification. The obfuscation technique therefore applies to quantum cryptographic algorithms as well.
verifications.gate_equivalence: sigma3 = Fredkin gate = CSWAP quantum gate

verifications.description: Classical cryptography relies on algebraic hardness (e.g., factoring). This approach instead uses PHYSICAL indeterminacy: the computation moves to a random location each run (space uncertainty), and the timing of activation differs per wire (time uncertainty). Like Heisenberg: you cannot know both WHERE the computation happens AND extract meaningful side-channel information from it. This is fundamentally different from complexity-theoretic security.
verifications.basis: Physical space-time uncertainty, not computational complexity

verifications.description: Because sigma3 gates physically route computation based on control bit S, a circuit built from sigma3 gates can redirect computation around faulty hardware components by adjusting control signals — without physically replacing any gates. This is analogous to network routing around failed nodes.
verifications.mechanism: Control bit S reroutes computation path around faulty gates
